summary: St. Francois County, MO Birch fire tower: an NGS datasheet dates it to 1938 and 1956; Forest Lookouts lists it as Removed and records a 1962 Conservation Commission land purchase.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as Removed; no removal date or method is given

evidence.supports: the header names St. Francois County and the Missouri Conservation Commission
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - St. Francois County - Missouri Conservation Commission

evidence.supports: the tower is listed as removed
in June 1962 the Conservation Commission acquired 194 acres for the Buck Mountain Tower site
evidence.quote: June 5, 1962: The Conservation Commission acquired 194 acres for the Buck Mountain Tower site.

evidence.supports: the survey mark is titled the Birch Fire Tower
the station is in St. Francois County, Missouri
the Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed the station in 1938
the tower was about 6 miles northeast of Ironton in the 1938 description
the 1938 description calls it a modest steel structure with a tub-shaped platform at the top
evidence.quote: TOWER IS A SMALL STEEL STRUCTURE WITH TUB-LIKE

evidence.supports: the 1938 description gives the tower as about 60 feet high
the 1956 recovery gives the condition as good
the 1956 recovery gives the tower as 50 feet high
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS OF STEEL CONSTRUCTION, 50 FEET HIGH

evidence.supports: the crow's nest on top is about four feet square
evidence.quote: FOOT SQUARE CROWS NEST ON TOP

evidence.supports: the 1956 recovery places the station in the Clark National Forest
the station marker is coded as a lookout tower

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed the station; the 1938 description gives the tower as about 60 feet high
Survey condition noted as GOOD; the 1956 recovery note gives the tower as 50 feet high with a crow's nest about four feet square and places the station in the Clark National Forest
Conservation Commission acquired 194 acres for the Buck Mountain Tower site, at a cost of $970

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts names the site Buck Mountain / Birch and the survey mark is titled Birch Fire Tower; both place a Birch-named tower in St. Francois County, so they are treated as one site

notes_for_editor: Unresolved height conflict: about 60 ft in the 1938 description versus 50 ft in the 1956 recovery, so height_m is omitted. Position: the NGS datasheet gives 37 39 50.44 N, which matches the record's latitude 37.664; longitude 90 31 48.00 W differs from the record's -90.5315 by about 0.0015 degree. Ownership: the 1956 note places the station in Clark National Forest and the 1962 purchase is the only later ownership note; no source explains the change. The Wikipedia Buck Mountain (St. Francois County) article did not mention a tower on a grep, so it is not used. Two searches found no removal record, staffing or fire history. Access, rental and any remains are not recorded. Confidence medium for identity and dates; low for fate.
